qt: to the Commission Siegbert Frank Droese (ESN) Subject:

The reform of the Central Securities Depositories Regulation (CSDR) is expected to enable the use of certain e-money tokens (EMTs) compliant with the Regulation on markets in crypto-assets (MiCA) for the settlement of the cash leg of securities transactions. Article 40 CSDR provides, in principle, for settlement in central bank money where practical and available. A matter that has not yet been expressly addressed is the issue, by a supervised intermediary, of an EMT that is fully backed by central bank deposits in a TARGET account. In such instances, the token is privately issued, but its reserves are 100 % central bank money. 1.
Under Article 40 CSDR, would the use of such an EMT constitute settlement in central bank money or EMTs?
If the latter, what is the regulatory significance of full backing by central bank money, particularly as regards de-risking, insolvency protection and the delivery-versuspayment link?

Does the Commission intend to expressly clarify the legal classification of EMTs fully backed by central bank money as part of the ongoing CSDR reform, whether in the legal text, in the recitals, or through the issue of technical standards or guidelines from the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) or the European Banking Authority (EBA)?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (16.11.2026) In accordance with Article 40 of the Central Securities Depositories Regulation (CSDR)1, central securities depositories (CSDs) are currently required to settle the cash leg of securities transactions through ‘accounts opened with a central bank’ or, under conditions, ‘through accounts opened with a credit institution’. From a legal point of view, the use of an electronic money token (EMT) issued by a credit institution cannot be considered settlement in central bank money even where that credit institution deposits the proceeds of issuing the EMTs on a Trans-European Automated Realtime Gross Settlement Express Transfer System (TARGET) account. As a result, the legal nature of an EMT is not changed by the fact that its funds are deposited on a TARGET account. To foster innovation, the Commission’s Market Integration and Supervision Package (MISP)2 proposes amending the CSDR to enable CSDs to settle the cash leg of securities transactions with certain EMTs regulated under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation3. In addition, the MISP also includes a definition of ‘central bank money’ to further differentiate between the possible ways to settle the cash leg of securities transactions including in the context of distributed ledger technology-based settlement. The proposal is currently under negotiation in the European Parliament and the Council. The Commission has also consulted on the review of the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation, including in relation to the regulatory framework for EMTs, and will communicate in due time on the possible way forward.
1 Regulation (EU) No 909/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 23 July 2014 on improving

securities settlement in the European Union and on central securities depositories and amending Directives 98/26/EC and 2014/65/EU and Regulation (EU) No 236/2012 (OJ L 257, 28.8.2014, p. 1, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2014/909/oj). 2 COM(2025) 943 final. 3 Regulation (EU) 2023/1114 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 31 May 2023 on markets in crypto-assets, and amending Regulations (EU) No 1093/2010 and (EU) No 1095/2010 and Directives 2013/36/EU and (EU) 2019/1937, OJ L 150, 9.6.2023, pp. 40–205, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/1114/oj .
